title: Role of Cyclohexanone Toxicity in Mediating Congenital Cardiac Surgery Outcomes
text:
We propose a new study to determine the role of cyclohexanone, an organic solvent
contaminant of medical plastics, in mediating adverse cardiovascular outcomes in neonatal cardiac surgery. We
will determine cyclohexanone and its breakdown products effect on test MP and validation U Michigan and
CATCH studies morbidity, mortality, and neurodevelopmental outcomes, determine mechanism of toxicity by
examining in vitro neural cell and brain slice culture, effects on the blood brain barrier and in vivo on learning
and memory and whether exposure can be reduced by CPB circuit manipulation. Reduction of organic solvent
exposure from medical plastics offers an opportunity for an immediate and actionable means to improve neonatal
cardiac surgical outcomes.

title: Mechanisms of somatic rescue in Fanconi anemia
text:
In Fanconi anemia (FA), aldehyde byproducts of endogenous metabolism create interstrand crosslinks in DNA
that promote dysfunction of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) that leads to the predominant
clinical manifestation of bone marrow failure (BMF) in childhood, and impaired enzymatic detoxification of
aldehydes exacerbates DNA damage and amplifies dysfunction of HSPCs. We performed whole exome
sequencing of human FA hematopoietic tissue compared to germline controls and identified a putative somatic
gain of function variant in the gene encoding the aldehyde clearance enzyme ALDH9A1 in an expanded HSPC
clone that improves the fitness of human FA hematopoietic cells when introduced into our disease models of
FA-associated BMF. In this proposal, we will investigate the potential therapeutic effect and underlying
mechanisms of transgenically and pharmacologically activating aldehyde clearance through ALDH9A1 in human
cell-based models of FA in culture and in vivo.

title: Dissecting the cooperation of FOXR2 and ETS transcription factors in FOXR2-expressing diffuse midline gliomas
text:
Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs) are devastating childhood brain tumors for which there are no effective
therapies. I previously identified aberrant FOXR2 expression as a key driver event in DMG formation and
growth, and that FOXR2 specifically activates ETS transcription factor circuits and is functionally redundant
with growth factor receptor pathways. The work proposed here seeks to define the mechanisms by which
FOXR2 cooperates with ETS transcription factors to drive MAPK signaling in FOXR2-expressing DMGs.

title: The Role of Peripheral Aged CD8+ T Cells in Hippocampal-Dependent Cognitive Decline
text:
The peripheral immune system has recently emerged as a potential driver of age-related cognitive impairments
and neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease, with a prominent role posited for CD8+ T cells.
Correspondingly, the research described in this proposal aims to investigate the role of circulating aged CD8+ T
cells and their secreted factors in driving hippocampal-dependent cognitive decline during aging. Completion of
this work will further the understanding of how age-associated changes in the peripheral immune system impact
the brain and ultimately identify potential therapeutic candidates to alleviate age-associated impairments in
cognition and susceptibility to neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease.

title: The Role of E3 Ligase MARCH10 in Influenza Virus Infection
text:
There are ~ 1 billion human influenza virus cases worldwide each year that cause up to 650,000 deaths.
Influenza virus infection remains difficult to treat because the antiviral drugs available are usually limited to
preventing influenza virus infection early in the infection and increasing drug resistance limits their
effectiveness. We have identified an E3 ligase MARCH10 that targets an influenza virus virulence factor for
degradation and propose in vitro and in vivo studies with the ultimate goal of developing new therapies to
combat influenza virus infection.

title: Probe-Based Light Sheet Microscopy (pLSM) for Screening of Anal Cancer
text:
We aim to significantly improve anal cancer screening, using a novel imaging tool termed probe-based light
sheet microscope (pLSM). The pLSM device non-invasively examines cellular details of anal tissues, which
can be used to provide high accuracy for diagnosing anal lesions. The pLSM image findings can guide the
clinician to areas concerning for precancer, which can increase the screening sensitivity and reduce the
morbidity caused by unnecessary biopsy of benign and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

title: Real-Time and Long-Term Effects of Medical Marijuana on Older Adults: A Prospective Cohort Study
text:
Older adults represent a fast-growing segment of medical marijuana (MM) users in this country, with chronic
pain as the most cited reason for use. There is a critical need to systematically examine MM’s short- and long-
term effects on the core outcomes of chronic pain including pain intensity, physical, emotional, and cognitive
functioning, and overall quality of life, and to track its side effects in older adults. This will be the first
prospective cohort study that innovatively combines technology-based ecological momentary assessments
(EMA) and in-person visits over 12 months to obtain both subjective and objective data on MM’s short- and
long-term effects on older adult with chronic pain.

title: Fixed-Target Platforms for Time-Resolved Crystallography
text:
X-ray crystallography is responsible for the majority of structural knowledge of biology at the molecular level.
However, most of this knowledge has been established by observing static endpoints related to macromolecular
function. We are developing novel fixed-target approaches to enable the next generation of serial time-resolved
X-ray crystallography experiments to directly probe structural dynamics and advance the field of structural
biology as a whole.

title: Role of OPA1 in Retinal Ganglion Cell Differentiation and the Pathogenesis of Dominant Optic Atrophy
text:
Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (DOA) is the most commonly diagnosed inherited optic neuropathy, and a
disease for which there is no treatment. We will use CRISPR/Cas9 based genome editing techniques and
human pluripotent stem cells to generate three new DOA models that track DOA disease progression from
stem cell differentiation to retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration. We propose to use these models to study
the role of OPA1 in RGC differentiation and degeneration.

title: Training in Cancer Genomics and Genomic Data Science
text:
Comprehensive analysis of the genomes of cancer cells is transforming our approach to the prevention,
diagnosis, and treatment of cancer. To date, however, the cancer genomics revolution has largely ignored tumors
from patients in Africa and has not involved many African scientists. The training program in this application aims
to provide graduate level training in cancer genomics and genomic data science to students in Uganda and East
Africa to prepare them to bring the benefit of the cancer genomics revolution to Africa.

title: The contribution of projection-specific endocannabinoid signaling in ethanol-related behaviors
text:
Since the COVID-19 pandemic, excessive alcohol consumption has become one of the leading causes of
preventable deaths in the United States. However, the projection-specific effects of ethanol on the
endocannabinoid system, a system implicated in regulating ethanol intake, is unclear. This project will answer
fundamental questions regarding how ethanol alters the endocannabinoid system, a neuromodulatory system in
the brain, at specific projections to elucidate the mechanisms underlying ethanol use.

title: Uncovering latent factors underlying weak and robust responses to influenza vaccine in healthy and obese older adults
text:
Bringing together teams from three complementary disciplines, vaccinology, immunology, and
systems biology, we propose to use novel methods for machine learning to examine multiple
immune parameters in older healthy weight and obese individuals who are weak and robust
responders to advanced-generation influenza vaccine. Analyses include single cell
transcriptional and chromatin (multi-ome) profiling of the innate and adaptive compartments,
cytokine profiling, multi-dimensional antibody profiling, and enumeration of HA-specific memory
B and plasma cell precursors. We will combine transcriptomic, epigenetic and cytokine datasets
to uncover both predictive correlates and causal latent factors of variable immunogenicity and
compare them between healthy weight and obese individuals.

title: Revealing the dynamics of RNA metabolism with nucleotide recoding chemistry
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health, because this work aims to illuminate the
diverse and dynamic mechanisms of RNA regulation in gene expression as well as how this
regulation is impacted by disease. As such, the proposed research is relevant to the part of the
NIH's mission that seeks to develop fundamental knowledge to inform our diagnosis and
treatment of human disease.

title: Enhancing PyLabRobot for Scalable and Accessible Open-Source Laboratory Automation
text: This project will expand PyLabRobot, an open-source platform that lets researchers and engineers design, simulate, and execute sophisticated laboratory automation workflows using Python—without the need for proprietary software or expensive hardware ecosystems. This research supports three key advances: a shared protocol repository for reproducible, AI-driven method development; cloud-based tools and an integrated development environment (IDE) to streamline accessibility; and a digital twin framework for predictive simulation and error reduction. By combining these innovations, we will accelerate biomedical research, reduce costs, and train a new generation of lab automation engineers critical to the U.S. biotech workforce and global competitiveness.

title: Rotavirus Genome Replication and Virion Assembly
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE STATEMENT (NARRATIVE):  
  
Rotaviruses are important causes of life-­threatening diarrhea in the young. This proposal will help us understand 
how  a  key  enzyme  of  rotavirus  functions  during  infection,  which  could  inform  antiviral  drug  design.  Thus,  the 
proposed  research  is  relevant  to  the part  of  NIH's  mission  that  pertains  to  creating knowledge  that will  help to 
reduce the burden of human disease.

title: Systematic PTM Knowledge Extraction and Evidence Quality Assessment in Alzheimer's Disease Research
text:
Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are critical in Alzheimer's disease, but over 10,000 annual publications
overwhelm manual curation. We will develop automated tools that extract PTM data from literature and score evidence
quality, creating a reliable knowledge base to accelerate drug target discovery.

title: High-Content Analysis to Accelerate Mechanistic and Therapeutic Identification for ABCA3 Deficiency
text:
Mutations in the ATP-binding cassette transporter A3 gene (ABCA3) are the most common genetic cause of
respiratory distress syndrome in full-term infants and interstitial lung disease among infants and children. As
effective medical treatment options remain limited, many affected patients require lung transplantation for
survival. We will use human lung cell lines to determine how specific ABCA3 mutations cause respiratory distress
syndrome and interstitial lung disease and to discover FDA-approved medications to treat affected infants and
children.

title: Tissue-Specific Regulation of Autophagy by PROPPINs
text:
Misregulation of autophagy has been implicated in numerous human diseases that stem from a variety of cell
and tissue types. Our proposal will elucidate how PROPPIN family members WIPI1-WIPI4 act synergistically
and independently in distinct cell types to regulate basal autophagy during development and maintenance of
function in adulthood. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to public health and the part of the NIH’s mission
that pertains to reducing illness and disability by identifying potential therapeutic targets for treating disparate
diseases.

title: Investigation of the neurobiological mechanisms underlying estradiol-mediated risk aversion in females
text:
Substance use disorder (SUD) is a costly and debilitating condition closely associated with poor decision making
and elevated risk taking. Although significant strides have been made toward identifying the neural mechanisms
by which substance use increases risk taking, the majority of this work is based on studies investigating the
neural substrates of risk taking in males; consequently, we have an impoverished understanding of the neural
substrates underlying risk taking in females, even before drug exposure. To begin to address this significant gap
in knowledge, the proposed work seeks to elucidate the neurobiological mechanisms underlying hormone-
dependent risk taking in females, the findings of which can then inform our understanding of how such
mechanisms may be compromised after chronic substance use in females and lead to elevated risk taking.

title: Research Project III: RNP-CRISPR to Treat Huntington's Disease
text: The experiments in this proposal focus on developing a therapy for Huntington's disease based upon Cas9 RNP formulations that are complexed to amphiphilic delivery peptides (ADPs) and conjugated to PEG. We have chosen Huntington's disease as a disease target because it is a fatal disease with no treatment, caused by a well-defined genetic mutation. CRISPR-based genome editing holds tremendous potential for treating Huntington's disease but has been challenging to develop because of delivery limitations. Two key challenges need to be solved before CRISPR-based genome editing can be used clinically. First, strategies for efficiently and safely delivering Cas9 and gRNA into neurons, after an intracranial injection, need to be developed. Second, strategies that can enable large volumes of brain tissue (>1 cm) to be transfected after an intracranial injection of CRISPR reagents must also be developed. This is particularly important for genome editing in large animals because charged macromolecules, such as Cas9 enzymes or viruses, typically only diffuse 1–2 mm away from the injection site after an intracranial injection. We have recently developed a new strategy for performing genome editing in the brain using a combination of convection-enhanced delivery (CED) combined with the Cas9 RNP complexed to new rationally designed amphiphilic delivery peptides (ADPs). This new strategy for Cas9 RNP delivery has shown remarkable promise, and was able to edit as much as 40% of the neurons in the vicinity of the injection site, after an intracranial injection, using the Ai9 mouse model. In addition, we have also demonstrated that conjugation of PEG to the Cas9 RNP dramatically enhances its distribution through brain tissue. Our Cas9 RNP + ADP formulations have much higher brain transfection ability than other strategies based upon just the Cas9 RNP fused to ADPs or nanoparticle based delivery methods. In addition, our formulation is based upon the Cas9 RNP, PEG and a well- defined peptide, and is anticipated to be significantly easier to manufacture than viral or nanoparticle-based formulations, as all the components – protein, gRNA, PEG, and peptide – can readily be produced under GMP conditions and have a robust clinical track record. In this proposal, we will build upon the momentum of our ongoing studies and will develop a Cas9 RNP formulation that can edit >50% of the mutant Huntington's gene after a single intracranial injection, administered via CED, using an RNP formulation that has the manufacturing and toxicology properties needed for performing IND-enabling studies. We propose the following aims: Specific Aim 1: Develop RNP monoparticles that efficiently transfect large volumes of brain tissue. Specific Aim 2. Rescue mice and rats from HD via editing of HTT using Cas9 RNP monoparticles. Specific Aim 3. Safety and process development of Cas9 RNP monoparticles.
